device_connectivity_online_explanation: This device requires an active internet connection to function. Setup, day-to-day control, or both rely on a manufacturer service. If the manufacturer's servers go offline or the product is discontinued, the device may stop working.
device_connectivity_offline_explanation: This device can be controlled locally on your home network. Keep in mind that "without the cloud" isn't always absolute: some devices may still need internet, a manufacturer account for setup, or the cloud for certain features.
device_connectivity_unknown_explanation: We don't yet have connectivity data for this device, so we can't say whether it depends on the manufacturer's cloud. This page will update as more reports come in.
device_ha_connect_body: Home Assistant is free software for running your smart home from a single app. To add this device, open Home Assistant, go to Settings > Devices and services, and click Add integration.
device_stats_note: Anonymized telemetry from opt-in Home Assistant users. No accounts, no personal data, no tracking.
about_lede: The Device Database is a project of the Open Home Foundation, the non-profit stewards of Home Assistant, ESPHome, Music Assistant, and friends.
about_body: It is built and maintained in the open. Manufacturer specs say what a device should do. We record what it actually does, drawn from anonymized data the community shares, and kept editorially neutral.
about_read_suffix: to see exactly what is shared, and how it is protected.
hiw_lede: Manufacturer specs say what a device should do. The Device Database tracks what it actually does, built from anonymized real-world data shared by the community.
hiw_step_1_body: Home Assistant users opt in to share what devices they run and how those devices behave. No personal data, no identifiers, no addresses.
hiw_step_2_body: Submissions are validated, then aggregated. A device only appears once enough independent contributions have been received.
hiw_step_3_title: Anyone can look it up, no account needed
hiw_step_3_body: You don't have to use Home Assistant to benefit. The Device Database is free, open, and built to help you make more informed decisions.
hiw_entry_body_1: Each device page aims to answer the questions that matter most when choosing a device, including compatibility, whether it requires an internet connection, which Home Assistant integration controls it, and what others have actually experienced running it, good or bad.
hiw_entry_body_2: Where a claim is unverified, the entry says so explicitly. Where the device works one way on one firmware and a different way on another, both are noted. The goal is editorial neutrality and source-backed precision, not marketing copy.
hiw_contribute_prefix: For now, the best way to contribute is to
hiw_contribute_link: opt in to Device Analytics in Home Assistant
hiw_contribute_suffix: . Every submission helps grow the database and improve the data available to everyone.
hiw_contribute_roadmap_prefix: Direct contributions to device pages, such as adding context, correcting details, or sharing first-hand experience, are on our
hiw_contribute_roadmap_suffix: . We're starting light: the immediate focus is making the device data collected so far accessible and useful to everyone through the Preview edition of this website.
hiw_contribute_discussion_suffix: and help shape the future of the Device Database.
editorial_lede: There are no good or bad devices. Only different capabilities, compatibilities, and trade-offs.
editorial_intro: This is a living resource. As community contributions grow and real-world usage evolves, so does what the database knows. We build in the open, share our methodology, and invite scrutiny. Trustworthiness is earned, not claimed.
editorial_body_1: The Device Database is a reference, not a marketing surface. We list what a device does, not what we think about it. Entries are written in the voice of a wiki editor, declarative, source-backed, and explicit about uncertainty. We give you the facts to make your own informed decisions.
editorial_body_2: There are no sponsored placements and no recommendation rankings. If a device requires the cloud, we say so plainly. If a claim is unverified, help us mark it.
editorial_body_3: The Device Database is a project of the Open Home Foundation, the non-profit stewards of Home Assistant, ESPHome, Music Assistant, and friends.
editorial_voice_body_1: Neutral and factual. State what a device does, not what we think about it. "The sensor reports presence using mmWave radar", not "this is a great presence sensor."
editorial_voice_body_2: Acknowledge uncertainty explicitly. "Reported to work, unverified." "This claim has no source, please add one." Trust is built by being honest about gaps.
editorial_voice_body_3: Verbs over adjectives. "Exposes 14 entities" beats "powerful entity support."
